question.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-y+2z=6 \\ 3x+2y-z=k \\ 4x+3y-3z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $x=1$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-9,$ find the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}|=-9\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}6 & -1 & 2 \\ k & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}| & =6\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}k & -1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}k & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =6(-6+3)+(-3k+1)+2(3k-2) \\  & =-18-3k+1+6k-4 \\  & =3k-21.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{3k-21}{-9}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $x=1.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-9}{3k-21} & =1 \\ -9 & =3k-21 \\ 12 & =3k \\ k & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
